How EDFM organizes Engineering reference material, relationships, and procedures.

== Purpose ==
Engineering is a connected subject area, but each article still has one clear owner. The [[Engineering]] hub introduces the system and routes readers to its major branches. Individual pages then cover Engineers, blueprints, Experimental Effects, materials, modules, or procedures without repeating one another in full.

This structure follows [[Elite Dangerous Field Manual:Editorial Policy#Topic ownership and page scope|EDFM's topic-ownership policy]].

== Page types and content ownership ==
{| class="wikitable"
! Page type !! Primary role !! Owns
|-
| [[Engineering]] || System hub || A concise overview of Engineering, its major concepts, and routes to the detailed reference and procedure pages.
|-
| [[Engineers]] || Directory || A comparison and navigation index for individual Engineers.
|-
| Individual Engineer articles || Reference || The Engineer's identity, location, discovery and meeting requirements, unlock requirement, services, maximum grades, version requirements, and direct referrals.
|-
| [[Engineering Blueprints]] and individual blueprint articles || Reference || Blueprint mechanics, grades, effects, costs, compatible modules, and Engineers who offer the blueprint.
|-
| [[Experimental Effects]] and individual effect articles || Reference || Effect behaviour, trade-offs, compatibility, and availability.
|-
| [[Engineering Materials]] and individual material articles || Reference || Material classification, sources, uses, and acquisition information specific to that material.
|-
| Module articles under [[Ships and Equipment]] || Reference || The module's normal specifications and behaviour together with its compatible Engineering options.
|-
| [[Engineer Unlock Guide]] and individual unlock guides || Procedure || Preparation, travel, acquisition steps, warnings, troubleshooting, and completion checks for reaching or unlocking Engineers.
|}

== Engineer articles ==
An Engineer article explains that Engineer. It retains concise requirements because discovery, meeting, and unlock conditions are part of the Engineer's identity and availability.

A short requirement such as delivering a named commodity belongs on the Engineer page. The full process for obtaining that commodity belongs on its commodity and activity pages, with links from the unlock procedure where needed.

Engineer articles may list direct referrals involving that Engineer. Large referral-chain walkthroughs belong in the relevant unlock guide or directory. General blueprint mechanics, Experimental Effect explanations, material gathering, Remote Workshop instructions, Engineering strategy, and build recommendations remain separate subjects.

== Blueprints and Experimental Effects ==
Each blueprint or Experimental Effect has one canonical article. A blueprint that applies to several modules is not split into separate pages for every module. Its page lists compatible modules and the Engineers who offer it, while each module article links back to the Engineering options available for that module.

This keeps blueprint values and compatibility information in one place and avoids conflicting copies across Engineer and module pages.

== Modules ==
A module has one reference article shared with [[Ships and Equipment]]. That article owns the module's stock specifications, operation, limitations, and compatible Engineering options.

Engineer pages may state that an Engineer modifies the module and to what maximum grade. They do not repeat the module's full specifications or every effect of its blueprints. Engineering procedures may name a required module but leave its detailed operation to the module article.

== Materials and acquisition procedures ==
[[Engineering Materials]] organizes Raw, Manufactured, and Encoded Materials. Individual material pages own material-specific source information and uses.

A material page may identify activities capable of producing the material. Complete collection routes, farming loops, mining workflows, and trading procedures belong in dedicated guides. Engineer unlock guides link through that chain instead of embedding unrelated activity tutorials.

== Unlock procedures and referrals ==
An Engineer article states the direct requirement for access. A dedicated unlock procedure explains how to satisfy it from beginning to end, including prerequisites, acquisition steps, travel, hand-in requirements, common mistakes, and expected results.

Referral relationships remain concise on individual Engineer pages and may be summarized in the [[Engineers]] directory. A procedure may cover a longer referral route when following that route is the task itself.

== Naming and navigation ==
Engineering articles use flat, human-readable Main-namespace titles such as [[Broo Tarquin]], [[Overcharged]], [[Thermal Vent]], and [[Multi-Cannon]]. They do not use artificial paths such as <code>Engineering/Blueprints</code> or duplicate Engineering-only module pages.

Every Engineering page links naturally to its parent hub and directly related subjects. The normal reader paths are:

* Engineer to unlock procedure to required commodity or activity;
* module to blueprint or Experimental Effect;
* blueprint to compatible modules and offering Engineers; and
* material to source activity to acquisition procedure.

Use {{tl|Engineering nav}} for consistent movement between the main Engineering hubs. Descriptive links in the article body remain preferable when a related page is needed to understand the text.

== Templates and structured data ==
Templates, infoboxes, Scribunto modules, and structured records may hold reusable Engineering data. Reader-facing prose presents that data as normal game information without exposing storage or implementation details.

Structured data should have one canonical source. Article prose may summarize it where that improves understanding, but it must not create a second manually maintained copy that can drift from the structured record.

New reference and procedure pages follow [[Elite Dangerous Field Manual:Creating an Article]] and [[Elite Dangerous Field Manual:Creating a Guide]]. Drafting placeholders and internal implementation commentary must be removed before a page is ready for readers.
